part.text: I’ve filtered to crashes dated Jan 1, 2013–Dec 31, 2025. I’m comparing total crash counts by weekday with the average count per occurrence of each weekday, since totals can be affected slightly by how often each weekday appears in the date range.

input.patchText:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: out/.generate_weekday.py
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")
+START = "2013-01-01"
+END = "2025-12-31"
+ORDER = ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"]
+
+con = duckdb.connect()
+rows = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT strftime(crash_date, '%A') AS weekday, COUNT(*) AS crashes
+    FROM read_parquet('data/crashes.parquet')
+    WHERE crash_date BETWEEN DATE ? AND DATE ?
+    GROUP BY weekday
+    """,
+    [START, END],
+).fetchdf()
+calendar_days = pd.date_range(START, END, freq="D")
+day_counts = calendar_days.day_name().value_counts()
+values = rows.set_index("weekday").reindex(ORDER).reset_index()
+values["crashes"] = values["crashes"].astype("int64")
+values["calendar_days"] = [int(day_counts[name]) for name in ORDER]
+values["share_of_crashes_pct"] = values["crashes"] / values["crashes"].sum() * 100
+values["average_crashes_per_weekday_date"] = values["crashes"] / values["calendar_days"]
+
+chart_specs = [
+    (1, "crashes", "Police-reported crashes", "Total crashes", "values_1.csv"),
+    (2, "average_crashes_per_weekday_date", "Crashes per calendar date", "Average crashes per occurrence of weekday", "values_2.csv"),
+]
+for option_id, column, ylabel, title, csv_name in chart_specs:
+    values.to_csv(OUT / csv_name, index=False, float_format="%.6f")
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5.2))
+    bars = ax.bar(values["weekday"], values[column], color="#3b78a6")
+    ax.set_title(f"{title}, NYC ({START[:4]}–{END[:4]})")
+    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
+    ax.set_xlabel("Day of week")
+    ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=25)
+    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+    ax.bar_label(bars, fmt="%.0f" if option_id == 1 else "%.1f", padding=3)
+    fig.tight_layout()
+    fig.savefig(OUT / f"option_{option_id}.png", dpi=160)
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+print(values.to_string(index=False, float_format=lambda x: f"{x:.3f}"))
*** End Patch
